long_biography.plain_text:
Green Mountain Coffee founder Robert Stiller encouraged employees to redesign how the business worked. Staff formed an environmental committee, improved shipping boxes and developed a policy against leaving delivery vehicles idling. He supported joint decision-making and invested in training that ranged from productivity skills to household budgeting.

Community work became part of the working week. Employees received an hour off to volunteer and could accumulate that time; one used a week to help a coffee-growing community in Costa Rica. Stiller also promoted appreciative inquiry, a management approach that asks people to identify strengths and build improvements from what an organisation already does well.
